question: Do the fixed note-profile methods reduce root errors on previously unevaluated recordings containing chord changes?
data: All 64 IDMT archive dataset4/acoustic_mic/fast files, subject to source and annotation preflight.
comparison_scope: New tempo performances of the same 64 pieces as the earlier slow-stream comparison. This is within-repertoire transfer, not new-song or new-progression generalization.
selection_rule: Include the complete fast acoustic-microphone stream; do not choose by labels, coverage or recognizer scores. No exclusions based on outcome.
primary_metric: Duration-weighted majmin accuracy including the existing NC-to-N convention.
diagnostics: Root accuracy on supported chord intervals only; predicted N is an error.
Chord-only majmin accuracy; near-change accuracy; boundary scores.
Wrong-root and same-root quality error durations; reference-N accuracy.
Scores by piece and total complete inference time.
settings: Use the exact three configurations already frozen on November 9. No further tuning from this comparison.
runtime: Single CPU thread, feature caching disabled, complete audio-to-decoded-interval wall time. Include file read, resampling, tuning, dictionary construction and fitting. Exclude imports, separate warm-up, scoring and output. Retain OS file cache.
analysis: One fixed comparison. Record all methods and adverse outcomes. Do not interpret shared repertoire or repeated performances as independent new songs.
expected_data_readiness: Source guide must support separately recorded tempi and local annotations must match all64fast filenames.
